to extend enterprise security to Codex agents and integrate OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Cyber into the Falcon platform. The collaboration aims to secure AI agents at the point of execution while using advanced cyber reasoning to help customers assess risks and prioritize security actions with greater speed, precision and scale.
Apart from this, CrowdStrike unveiled the next evolution of

, introducing coordinated multi-agent investigations across endpoint, identity, SaaS, cloud and network environments. The technology enables AI agents to investigate threats at machine speed, reducing investigations that once took hours to minutes while delivering trusted verdicts for security teams.

CrowdStrike also launched Falcon Guardian, an evolution of its AIDR platform that provides AI visibility and runtime security at the endpoint. The solution enables real-time detection and response to attacks and malicious activity involving AI agents.

The company also introduced Real-Time Supply Chain Attack Protection, a new Falcon platform capability that blocks malicious open-source packages at the endpoint before embedded code can execute. As AI coding agents rapidly pull packages from public registries, the solution intercepts poisoned packages during installation, helping prevent malicious code from running and gaining access to endpoints.

attended CrowdStrike’s Fal.Con 2026 in Las Vegas and reported positive customer and partner sentiment, with vendor consolidation and demand for AI Detection and Response (AIDR) emerging as key tailwinds.

Most large customers spoken with had expanded their CrowdStrike footprint, particularly in Next-Gen SIEM and Vulnerability/Exposure Management, while two customers reported positive experiences with AIDR, said the analyst.
The analyst remained bullish on the company with a Buy rating and price forecast of $245.
CrowdStrike Holdings shares were down 5.48% at $203.29 at the time of publication Wednesday.
